newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Liberals offering access for donors - paper.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Liberals offering access for donors - paper.

text.p: Canada's ruling Liberal Party has sent out letters suggesting big donors could get special access to Prime Minister Jean Chretien, the Globe and Mail reported on Friday.
The report immediately drew comparisons with U.S. President Bill Clinton inviting wealthy supporters over for coffee or overnight stays in the Lincoln Bedroom at the White House.

"In a letter to prospective donors, the party's elite Laurier Club talked of a get-together in the near future with cabinet ministers and a summer-time party at Mr. Chretien's official residence ... along with invitations to Liberal conventions," the Toronto-based newspaper said.
It added that the letter was sent out last week, three days before Chretien called a June 2 federal election. Club membership was set at C$1,000 (U.S. $700) a year, it said.

Liberal Party officials were unable to provide a copy of the letter or confirm the exact contents. But Sean Kirby, a spokesman at the Liberal campaign headquarters in Ottawa, said all parties raise money in a similar way.

"Party fund-raising is something that all parties do, and it's obviously necessary. Without it our political system doesn't work," Kirby told Reuters, adding that Chretien was also accessible at other events.
"It's something that's gone on, always has gone on and is, you know, pretty accepted practice."
He said the Laurier Club had been around for years and hundreds of people went to its social events.
"If it gets close to selling access to the prime minister, that's really something that shouldn't be for sale," Preston Manning, leader of the Reform Party, told a news conference in Calgary.
"You know how Bill Clinton got into trouble by putting up people in Lincoln's bed, and that was frowned upon by commentators and Americans, and I think Canadians would feel the same."
